target_customer: Startups and small companies hiring contract-to-hire marketing, design and operations talent; originally startups hiring college students
problem: Hiring a full-time employee blind is risky; trying someone on a project first (contract-to-hire) is hard to arrange. Originally, startups struggled to hire college student freelancers.
business_model: Marketplace: 15% take on transaction volume plus SaaS fees from some companies in 2020 (TechCrunch); later a commission-free talent marketplace (2025 company blog)
product_category: Talent marketplace for fractional and contract-to-hire work

founders.name: Adam Alpert
founders.background_notes: YC page: started as a freelance videographer in middle school; featured in TechCrunch, Boston Globe and Inc. Magazine.

founders.name: John Tambunting
education: Brown University, Applied Mathematics degree (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Got into coding through college hackathons.

competitors.name: Upwork
competitors.what: General freelance marketplace, named on Pangea's own comparison pages

competitors.name: Fiverr
competitors.what: General freelance marketplace, named on Pangea's own comparison pages

technical_complexity.rationale: A two sided marketplace with profiles, matching and contracts; standard web engineering with a team of 3.

defensibility.rationale: Talent network of 70,000 (founder claim) gives some liquidity, but freelance marketplaces are copyable and compete with Upwork, Fiverr and Toptal.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying Pangea; Upwork partnered with Podium Education in 2024 to onboard students, a similar wedge.

market_need_then: In 2020-04 TechCrunch reported about 250 schools with students on the platform, five figures of contracts and 60 new schools in three weeks, as COVID reduced internships.

branding.domain_note: Uses pangea.app on the .app TLD; acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: Black and white logo versions per the 2025 blog
identity.voice_and_tone: Community language: Build with Pangeans, grow with Pangea

branding.brand_signature: Users and talent are called Pangeans

rebrands.why: Company blog says the college-only vision no longer matched the community it had formed; the name stayed the same

branding.community_and_virality: Talent community of 70,000 creatives per a founder profile (self reported); 1,500 campuses at peak per the 2025 blog.

brand_strength.rationale: Pangea is a common word shared with many companies, though the Pangeans community term gives some identity; press was limited to funding news.

pivots.to: Fractional and contract-to-hire talent marketplace for marketing and design with 0% talent fees
pivots.why: The college-only vision no longer represented the experienced community that had formed (company blog, updated 2025-04-05)

outcome_analysis: Pangea raised $400K in 2020-04 and a $2M seed in 2021-07 after the W21 batch, then shifted from college students to experienced fractional talent, announced in 2025-04. The company is still a team of 3 on the YC page, which suggests slow scaling despite claims of a large talent network. It competes with Upwork, Fiverr and Toptal, so differentiation rests on contract-to-hire.
notes: The $2M seed is confirmed by Pangea's own blog title and press page, a TechCrunch repost (pipedot), and the YC page link to TechCrunch dated 2021-07-29; CB Insights gives 2021-07-07. The investor list for the seed comes from CB Insights (aggregator) and the careers page. Aggregator totals ($2.89M, $3.0M, $3.3M in a YC job post) exceed the recorded $2.4M, so coverage is partial. A blog entry dated 2025-04-05 titled Raises $2MM Seed Round appeared in search results; it was not opened and is probably the 2021 post re-dated. Co-founder Isaac Zussman appears in one search summary only and is not listed. The competitor list uses Pangea's own comparison pages, which are undated, because no dated 2020 to 2021 source was found; student marketplaces Stint, Clutch and Hustlance appeared in undated results. Founded 2016 per the YC page.
